questions.question: Give the names and formulae of the four common acids and five common bases required by the syllabus, and state one household or industrial identity for each acid.
questions.expected_answer: The acids: hydrochloric acid, HCl — stomach acid and pool acid; nitric acid, HNO₃ — the acid of fertiliser manufacture; sulphuric acid, H₂SO₄ — car battery acid; and ethanoic (acetic) acid, CH₃COOH — the acid in vinegar. The bases: sodium hydroxide, NaOH (caustic soda); potassium hydroxide, KOH; ammonia, NH₃ (in household cleaners); sodium carbonate, Na₂CO₃ (washing soda); and sodium hydrogen carbonate, NaHCO₃ (baking soda or bicarbonate of soda).

questions.question: Explain, using ionic charges, why sulphuric acid is H₂SO₄ but nitric acid is HNO₃, and why sodium carbonate is Na₂CO₃ but sodium hydrogen carbonate is NaHCO₃. Then explain why sulphuric acid is called diprotic while ethanoic acid, with four hydrogens in its formula, is monoprotic.
questions.expected_answer: A formula must have charges totalling zero. Sulphate is SO₄²⁻, so its double negative charge needs two H⁺ ions: H₂SO₄. Nitrate is NO₃⁻ with a single negative charge, needing only one H⁺: HNO₃. Carbonate is CO₃²⁻ and needs two Na⁺ ions: Na₂CO₃. Hydrogen carbonate, HCO₃⁻, has already gained one hydrogen, which neutralises one of the two negative charges, so its single remaining minus needs only one Na⁺: NaHCO₃. Sulphuric acid is diprotic because it can release both of its hydrogen ions in water. Ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH, is monoprotic because only the hydrogen bonded to oxygen at the end of the formula is acidic; the three hydrogens in the CH₃ group are bonded to carbon and are never released. It is also a weak acid, releasing even its one available hydrogen incompletely.

questions.question: State the general products of a neutralisation reaction and the rule that connects a salt's name to its parent acid and base. Then choose an acid and a base to prepare potassium sulphate, and write the balanced equation for sodium hydroxide neutralising sulphuric acid.
questions.expected_answer: Acid plus base gives a salt plus water. The salt's positive ion (its first name, the metal) comes from the base, and its negative ion (its surname) comes from the acid: hydrochloric acid gives chlorides, nitric acid gives nitrates, sulphuric acid gives sulphates and ethanoic acid gives ethanoates. To prepare potassium sulphate, choose potassium hydroxide as the base and sulphuric acid as the acid: potassium supplies the salt's first name and sulphate is sulphuric acid's family name. For sodium hydroxide and sulphuric acid: 2NaOH + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O — two sodium hydroxide react per sulphuric acid because the diprotic acid has two hydrogens to neutralise, producing sodium sulphate and two water molecules.
